taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1. Pacific Time (PT) is UTC-7 during standard time (not daylight saving). However, October 24, 2026, falls after the U.S. daylight saving time ends (which is on the first Sunday in November), so on October 24, 2026, PT will be UTC-7 (standard time).

So:  
- Deadline in PT: Friday, October 30, 2026, 11:59 PM PT = UTC-7  
- Convert to UTC: 11:59 PM + 7 hours = 06:59 UTC on Saturday, October 31, 2026  
- Convert to Madrid (CET = UTC+1): 06:59 UTC + 1 hour = 07:59 CET on Saturday, October 31, 2026

Wait — let’s double-check the date logic.

Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026.  
Six days from today is Friday, October 30, 2026.  
So deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026, 11:59 PM PT.

Now convert October 30, 2026, 23:59 PT (UTC-7) to Madrid time (UTC+1):

Difference: UTC+1 - (UTC-7) = 8 hours ahead.

So: 23:59 PT + 8 hours = 07:59 on Saturday, October 31, 2026.

Yes — because when it’s 11:59 PM Friday in PT, it’s already 7:59 AM Saturday in Madrid.

So the local deadline in Madrid is Saturday, October 31, 2026, at 07:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Los Angeles is in the Pacific Time Zone (PT). On October 30, 2026, Daylight Saving Time ends in the U.S. on November 1, so on October 30, Los Angeles is still on PDT (UTC-7). Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) in October 2026 (since DST in Europe ends on October 25, 2026, so CEST is still in effect).

So:
- Los Angeles (PDT): UTC-7
- Madrid (CEST): UTC+2
- Time difference: 9 hours ahead in Madrid.

Deadline in Los Angeles: Monday, November 2, 2026, at 10:00 AM PDT.

Convert to Madrid time: Add 9 hours → 10:00 + 9 = 19:00 (7:00 PM) on the same day.

So deadline in Madrid: Monday, November 2, 2026, at 19:00.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts on Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours.  
Adding 48 hours to the start time:  
- 24 hours later is Sunday, October 25, 2026 at 18:00  
- Another 24 hours later is Monday, October 26, 2026 at 18:00  

Since the event is in Madrid time and you’re in Madrid, the end time is in your local time.  

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT (Pacific Time) is UTC-7 during daylight saving time (PDT) and UTC-8 during standard time. October 26, 2026 is after the end of daylight saving time in the U.S. (which occurs on the first Sunday in November), so on October 26, 2026, PT will be UTC-8 (PST).

So, 10:00 AM PT on October 26, 2026 = 18:00 UTC.

Madrid is in Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1 in standard time. Since October 26, 2026 is after the end of daylight saving time in Europe (last Sunday in October), Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1).

Therefore, 18:00 UTC = 19:00 Madrid time.

The deadline is 72 hours later: 19:00 + 72 hours = 19:00 on October 29, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Submissions close on October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (Eastern Time).  
36 hours after that is November 2, 2026 at 11:59 AM ET.

Madrid is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1 (or UTC+2 during daylight saving).  
Spain observes Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) from late March to late October.  
October 31, 2026 is a Saturday — daylight saving ends on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026.  
So on October 31, 2026, Spain is on CET (UTC+1), not CEST.

ET (Eastern Time) is UTC-5 during standard time (which begins on November 1, 2026).  
Wait — daylight saving ends in the US on November 1, 2026 at 2:00 AM, so on October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET, the US is still on EDT (UTC-4).

So:  
- October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM EDT = UTC 03:59 (November 1, 2026)  
- 36 hours later: UTC 15:59, November 2, 2026  
- Madrid is on CET (UTC+1), so local time = UTC+1 = 16:59 on November 2, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The Unix timestamp 1791788340 represents the number of seconds since January 1, 1970, UTC.

Converting this timestamp to UTC:
- 1791788340 seconds = ~56.8 years since 1970
- Using a standard converter: 1791788340 UTC = **2027-06-10 12:59:00 UTC**

Tokyo is in the Japan Standard Time (JST) zone, which is UTC+9.

So, add 9 hours to UTC:
- 12:59 UTC + 9 hours = 21:59 JST

Therefore, the deadline in Tokyo local time is:

ANSWER: 2027-06-10 21:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid, Spain observes Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) in winter and Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) in summer. The deadline is on October 25, 2026.

October 25, 2026 is after the last Sunday of October, when Spain reverts from daylight saving time (CEST) back to standard time (CET). The clock change happens at 3:00 AM CEST → 2:00 AM CET on the last Sunday of October, which in 2026 is October 25.

So, at 2:30 UTC on October 25, 2026, Spain is still on CEST (UTC+2), because the switch happens at 3:00 AM CEST — meaning 2:30 UTC is still 4:30 AM local time in Madrid, before the clocks fall back.

Wait — correction: 2:30 UTC is 4:30 AM CEST (UTC+2) on October 25, 2026. The switch to CET occurs at 3:00 AM CEST, which is 2:00 UTC. So at 2:30 UTC, it is 4:30 AM in Madrid — still CEST. The switch happens *after* 2:30 UTC.

Therefore, 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z = 4:30 AM CEST in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 04:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026.  
Pacific Time (PT) is UTC-8 during standard time (after daylight saving ends).  
Daylight Saving Time in the U.S. ends on the first Sunday in November, so on October 25, 2026, Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7) is still in effect.  
Thus, 11:59 PM PDT on October 25, 2026 = 06:59 UTC on October 26, 2026.  

Madrid is in Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1 in standard time, but observes Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) from late March to late October.  
October 25, 2026 is still within CEST (since DST in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October — which is October 25 in 2026 — at 01:00 UTC, i.e., 03:00 CEST).  
So at 06:59 UTC on October 26, 2026, it is 08:59 CEST in Madrid.  

Therefore, the deadline in Madrid is 08:59 on October 26, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 08:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The U.S. ends daylight saving time on the first Sunday in November each year. In 2026, that is November 1, 2026.

At 12:00 noon Eastern Time (ET) on that day, it is standard time (EST), since daylight saving ends at 2:00 AM that morning, clock falling back to 1:00 AM.

Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time (PET) zone, which is UTC−5 year-round and does not observe daylight saving time.

Eastern Time (EST) is also UTC−5 during standard time.

Therefore, when it is 12:00 noon EST in the U.S., it is also 12:00 noon in Lima — same time zone.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is a time zone that ends at 12:00 UTC on the last day of the year — meaning 24:00 AoE on December 31, 2026, is equivalent to 12:00 UTC on January 1, 2027.

Tokyo is in the Japan Standard Time (JST) zone, which is UTC+9.

So, 12:00 UTC on January 1, 2027, is 21:00 JST on January 1, 2027.

Therefore, the deadline in Tokyo is 21:00 on January 1, 2027.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney (Australia) is in the Australian Eastern Time zone (AEST/AEDT). On October 5, 2026, Sydney will be on AEDT (UTC+11), since October is during daylight saving time in Australia.

New York (USA) is in Eastern Time (ET), which on that date will be EDT (UTC-4), since Daylight Saving Time is in effect in the US in October.

So, Sydney (UTC+11) is 15 hours ahead of New York (UTC-4).

Deadline: 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026  
→ Subtract 15 hours → 2:00 AM on October 5, 2026 in New York.

But wait — 5 PM minus 15 hours is 2 AM *same day*? Let’s check:

5:00 PM (17:00) - 15 hours = 02:00 on the same calendar day (October 5).

Yes, because 17 - 15 = 2.

So, 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026 = 2:00 AM New York time on October 5, 2026.

Since you’re in New York, that’s your local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
